However, these are expert witnesses, and the expertise follow certain international standards and now we have two experts that should actually confront each other on the basis of these different scientific grounds. Now, I do -- I am entitled to being a bit suspicious when an expert testifies as an expert as a member of the Prosecution. The more so because -- and I'm especially entitled to being a little bit suspicious of the portion of the work that was done by the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina experts because this is really a conflict of interest in their case. So please, I just want to make myself very clear, we are not in any way suggesting that the OTP experts are deliberately misleading or presenting false information. We just feel that in order to establish a certain level of confidence, we must verify certain things.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: One more point, the letter of Dr. Dunjic was actually very helpful, and we think we will not oppose cross-examination, but we would have to see this letter and have a possibility to digest it and consider it. It would be very helpful if we had something also from Dr. Stojkovic because he has already the 30 files with the raw material for one grave. If he could look at that and also give a preliminary assessment and if he finds points to make that would definitely be very helpful, then we could even deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I have a proposal. Let's simplify matters and speed up the whole proceeding. I've noticed that in some other cases, and this is something that other Trial Chambers had resorted to, the procedure would be that a certain witness will be -- that a certain witness report will be accepted in part as a credible report, whereas other portions are not admitted as being insufficiently credible. I feel that in the event -- in my view, it would be far more appropriate if there is any doubt as to an expert witness and the report of an expert witness, I believe that we should eliminate the entire report and the witness, and in this way we would probably eliminate some of the experts right off. Of course, I'm joking in part, but just in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one comment on what you said earlier about the work being done by the representatives of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Federation, I think all of the expert work here has been independently reviewed and presented by an international expert no doubt with a view to ensuring that the appropriate standards have been met. And you're quite right to identify the principal bases, as I see it, for attacking the expert evidence as the quality rather than the partiality of the work that's been done. Now, is there any other point on these expert matters that you, Dr. Karadzic, wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For now, no. I would just like to address you off record with one thing, but I would like to do that at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SLADOJEVIC
utterances.text: If I may, make one thing on behalf of Dr. Karadzic. In relation to the ICMP materials, now, we went through the testimony suggested, testimony of Dr. Parsons, as suggested by the OTP to find out about the mandate and organisation of the ICMP. So we went also to the website. We couldn't find many thing that we thought we would find, but anyway in them, ICMP -- Dr. Parsons claims the ICMP establishes neither the year nor the manner and time of the death, and which can be established according to our experts through the DNA analysis. So in addition to establishing the identities and the number of victims, we would also like to conduct independent analysis in order to try too establish through the DNA analysis the time of death which is also very important. Unfortunately I've only one memorandum that we prepared for this meeting in relation to the ICMP work, but I can send it by e-mail, if you want. I think it's more useful if you give it the Trial Chamber at this stage, as well in relation to the Serbian letters, Dr. Dunjic's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Retzlaff, Mr. Nicholls, anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will be meeting Dr. Kleiser, and we will ask him whether this is possible and whether they can do something in addition to time of death and cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would just add, Your Honour, just to be clear, the Defence now has their own communication with Dr. Kleiser and are working directly with ICMP, but we will continue to do anything we can to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I hope this meeting has assisted parties in identifying ways of speeding up this whole exercise in the interests of ensuring that injustice is avoided. I'm very grateful to you, Dr. Karadzic, for arranging for Mr. Sladojevic to attend this meeting. I've found that helpful. Although you, yourself, have a measure of knowledge of the subject, those who are actually carrying out the day-to-day dealings with the OTP usually have some information that would be supplementary to you, so that was of great assistance to this meeting. And if there's anything else discovered on the subject by the time of the Status Conference on Thursday then that can be raised, but I suspect there's nothing more to be said on this for the moment, and I just wish you well in trying to make progress in reviewing the expert evidence. Thank you very much. Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to tell you something that has nothing to do directly with the case, but it was not decent to say that in a public session -- has to do with Saint Andrew. I'm a Knight of Saint Andrew. He is also a protector of Russia, and it was not perhaps quite appropriate to say that and he is from Russia, I have a medal of Saint Andrews, and this is something that is perhaps not appropriate to state in a public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it you are referring to the fact that he is my patron saint. I doubt if it will work well in a Defence case though. Thank you. Until Thursday, thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Rule 65 ter Conference adjourned
